Alright, I've just applied a tweak to `agent.ts` to tighten up the narration logic – limiting the visible text length to 240 characters before emitting it, and clarifying the comment about holding back premature claims. The edit succeeded (the tool reported the file was updated). 

Now I need to assess the impact of this change on the overall system, particularly on the resource usage and cost metrics that Glint tracks. Since the agent runs in a tmux session named `glint`, the most straightforward way to get a current cost breakdown is to invoke the built‑in `/usage` command that prints a summary of token consumption, tool calls, and estimated cost. 

I could try to just read a log file, but the usage stats are dynamically generated and formatted by Glint’s command interface, so pulling them via the `/usage` command ensures I see the latest numbers. To do that, I need to send the appropriate keystrokes to the tmux pane: first the `C-t` shortcut (which opens the command prompt in Glint), then type `/usage`, press Enter, wait a moment for the output to render, and finally capture the pane contents. I only care about the final few lines where the cost breakdown appears, so I’ll pipe the capture through `tail -6`. 

Putting it together, the Bash command will be:
`tmux send-keys -t glint C-t && sleep 0.3 && tmux send-keys -t glint '/usage' && sleep 0.2 && tmux send-keys -t glint Enter && sleep 1 && tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -v '^\\s*$' | tail -6`

This will give me a clean view of the current usage stats right after my recent edit, letting me verify that the change hasn't caused any unexpected token bloat or cost increase. I’ll execute this now.
